summary: Robotics engineer working at the perception end. I build the layer that turns raw camera images into geometry, meaning and decisions for robots, then take it to the hardware and make it run in real time. Finishing a PhD in real-time monocular perception and 3D mapping for autonomous UAVs, across detection, semantic segmentation and monocular depth, from training through optimisation to deployment on Jetson-class devices. Before that I shipped a fine-tuned detector inside a live commercial product and built the navigation stack behind a fleet of more than 30 service robots.

experience.role: Doctoral researcher, robotics and computer vision
experience.note: PhD project: autonomous real-time UAV mapping with spatial perception for indoor applications. Supervised by George Vosselman and Francesco Nex.
bullets: Built Mono-Hydra++, a real-time monocular RGB and IMU pipeline that constructs hierarchical 3D scene graphs for indoor drone mapping. C++ extensions to the VIO backend add sparse depth factors for metric-aware pose graph estimation, cutting trajectory error by 61% on ScanNet against monocular GO-SLAM while holding 25 to 30 Hz.

Took the full perception and mapping stack from prototype to deployment on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX with TensorRT FP16, ROS integration, and runtime profiling, reaching 25 fps on device under real-time compute limits.

Developed M2H and M2H-MX, the multi-task perception frontends behind Mono-Hydra++, predicting metric depth and semantic labels jointly from a single image. M2H appeared at IEEE/RSJ IROS 2025; M2H-MX was accepted at the IEEE ICRA 2026 SRRA Workshop, improving NYUDv2 mIoU by 6.6% and depth RMSE by 9.4%.
Building an indoor UAV exploration system in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, where the drone plans over semantic scene graphs from Mono-Hydra++, with transfer to a custom-built drone for real-world validation.
